extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from diverse indoor and outdoor environments with depth and disparity labels. It was collected with two 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a LiDAR sensor, and includes an augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We built a custom rig and collected data across distinct scenes, encompassing indoor and outdoor settings in various lighting conditions on a university campus. The setup integrated two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras and an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, mounted on a custom-built, remotely controlled robot chassis, with synchronized capture managed by an embedded NVIDIA Jetson Xavier.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that depth completion was used to increase label density, and that regions with high uncertainty were filtered so original labels were retained rather than adding high-error labels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 29 video sequences collected with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras (4K/UHD equirectangular images at 30 fps) and an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor (10 fps, 64 beams), on indoor and outdoor campus scenes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To assess alignment accuracy, we calculated the pixel error by measuring Euclidean distances between 200 randomly selected LiDAR points and their image positions, resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels. When selecting the same number of points from visually challenging areas, the error remains relatively low at 8.0 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Depth completion was used to fill sparse LiDAR depth labels, producing dense depth labels in homogeneous regions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No explicit post-preprocessing data manipulation such as augmentation, balancing, or sampling is described in the provided section.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Unnecessary regions (sky, ground) were cropped from the data; sparse ground-truth evaluation was handled by masking to evaluate only pixels with available ground truth values, and regions with high uncertainty were filtered out.
